First-time user route. No prior interface knowledge is assumed. Every critical action includes an expected result, recovery and STOP condition.

1. What this seminar is and is not

This seminar studies a dashboard that aggregates three independent local sources. Your task is not merely to make the final screen look right. You must show who starts each request, how failures are classified, how the exact model is built and what your evidence cannot establish.

Roles: P01 is the 60-minute core. P02 is the required later portfolio. P03 is optional.

Optional official references: Chrome DevTools, Edge DevTools and Firefox Developer Tools. The guide remains fully functional offline.

2. Download, extract and identify the package

  1. Locate the ZIP

    WHERE YOU ARE: File Explorer or Finder.

    EXACT ACTION: Keep the downloaded ZIP intact until it is on your computer. Choose Extract All or the platform equivalent.

    WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE: A real folder containing VERIFY_PACKAGE, 00_START_HERE and 02_PROJECTS.

    STOP if the address bar still shows a compressed archive.

3. Verify integrity and environment

./VERIFY_PACKAGE.sh

WHAT YOU SHOULD SEE: PASS_PACKAGE_INTEGRITY_EXACT_SET. Then run ./CHECK_ENVIRONMENT.sh or the matching Windows launcher.

WHAT TO RECORD: PACKAGE_ID, operating system, Node and npm versions and the exact MATCH/MISMATCH/ABSENT classification.

STOP on any missing, extra or modified package file. A runtime mismatch is recorded honestly and uses the offline route; it is not silently accepted.

4. Preserve the P01 fixture prediction

Open only these three files: profile.json, tasks.json and notices.json. Before running the project, write the predicted profile, open/total count, notice count and state transition.

Reveal the fixture key only after saving your prediction

Ada, Web Lab, two open tasks out of three, two notices, loading then success.

Do not continue unless the prediction names the exact fixture files. Do not rewrite it after seeing the result.

5. Verify the starter signature and edit boundary

./VERIFY_INITIAL_STATE.sh

P01 must report baseline PASS, exactly three named objective assertion failures and regression PASS. A parse error, timeout, crash, missing command or changed protected file is a real failure.

Edit only 02_PROJECTS/P01_MULTI_SOURCE_DASHBOARD/public/dashboard.js.

6. Implement loading and independent initiation

Render { state: "loading" } first. Then create all three request promises before awaiting the aggregate.

Three requests that reach the same destination are not automatically concurrent; they may be a sequential queue wearing a dashboard trench coat.

DO NOT CONTINUE UNLESS: the deferred observer shows all three paths in called before the first release.

7. Classify transport, HTTP and parsing

A network rejection means no usable Response was obtained. An HTTP 404 normally fulfils with ok=false. JSON parsing can fail after a successful status.

STOP if non-ok HTTP is parsed as successful data or indefinite loading remains visible.

8. Verify success, edge and error paths

./TEST_P01.sh

The exact success model contains state, profile, openTaskCount, totalTaskCount and notices. An empty tasks array is success with 0/0.

OUTPUT VERSUS MECHANISM: sequential awaits may produce the same final model. Use the deferred witness to distinguish the mechanism.

9. Start and stop the loopback project safely

./START_P01.sh

Copy the exact printed http://127.0.0.1:<port> URL. Do not guess a port. Use STOP_PROJECT when finished.

10. Inspect Network and DOM in your browser

Chrome

Select the three-dot menu to the right of the address bar, then More tools → Developer tools. Select Network.

Edge

Select Settings and more (…), then More tools → Developer tools. Select Network.

Firefox

Select the hamburger menu, then More tools → Web Developer Tools. Select Network.

WHAT TO RECORD: browser/version, local URL, one request/status, visible DOM state and an explicit limit.

11. Audit one Gemini claim

Open a new tab, visit Gemini Web, start a new chat and check that the excerpt contains no credentials, cookies, Moodle data, personal data or private code.

Review this bounded claim about the supplied S04 dashboard. Do not assume it is correct.

Claim: Starting the profile request, awaiting it, then starting tasks and notices is equivalent to starting all three before awaiting because the final dashboard values are the same.

Return exactly: (1) claim restatement, (2) what is observed, inferred or unknown, (3) one discriminating test, (4) ACCEPTED, REJECTED, PARTIALLY ACCEPTED or UNKNOWN, (5) correction and (6) explicit limit. Do not request private data.

If Gemini is unavailable, use the supplied synthetic claim only as offline practice. Do not describe it as a real interaction.

12. Hand off to the required P02 portfolio

Preserve a prediction about direct checkbox clicks, nested Delete clicks and callback changes after cleanup. Complete P02 after the core hour by editing only public/task-view.js.

Do not begin a second complete implementation inside the 60-minute core.

13. Complete the form and one final PDF

Open FORM_S04_EN_GB.html with OPEN_MOODLE_FORM. The form saves locally, exports/imports JSON and prints without sending data.

Use the recommended filename TW2026_S04_GROUP_Surname_Firstname.pdf. Include P01 and the required P02 portfolio.

14. Submit to Moodle and verify the status

  1. Open the correct course, week and Assignment.
  2. Verify the title before uploading.
  3. Choose Add submission or the local equivalent.
  4. Upload exactly one PDF and wait until the filename is visible.
  5. Select Save changes.
  6. If shown, select Submit assignment and confirm.
  7. Verify final status, filename and timestamp.

STOP if the status remains Draft. Moodle labels are planning guidance until verified on the live institutional instance.

15. Troubleshooting wizard and glossary

Select a symptom.
initiation
Creating or starting an asynchronous operation.
completion
The point at which an operation fulfils or rejects.
HTTP non-success
A Response exists, but response.ok is false.
transport rejection
No usable Response is obtained.
injected witness
A controlled substitute that exposes a mechanism without claiming browser evidence.
event delegation
One ancestor listener resolves actions from descendant targets.
